newsitem.title: DUBAI: PLO's Arafat hold talks in UAE on Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat hold talks in UAE on Mideast peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday for talks on the deadlocked Middle East peace process, the official WAM news agency said.

Arafat, who came to the UAE on the second leg of a Gulf tour, met with Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Sultan bin Zaid al-Nahayan and discussed "the latest developments in the Middle East in light of the stalled peace process", the agency said.
Sheikh Sultan reaffirmed his country's support for the Palestinian cause, WAM said.
He also emphasised the UAE's disapproval of a U.S. House of Representatives recommendation to President Bill Clinton to reaffirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital.
"He said the recommendation damaged the peace process," WAM said. UAE officials had previously said the proposal cast doubts over Washington's neutrality in the Middle East peace process.
The Palestinian president arrived in the UAE from Saudi Arabia, where he had held talks with King Fahd, Crown Prince Abdullah and Defence Minister Prince Sultan.
Arafat presented all three men with medals for their service to the Palestinian people, Saudi television said.
Arafat last visited Saudi Arabia in December.
Saudi-PLO relations, which soured during the 1991 Gulf War due to the PLO's support for Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, have improved since the 1993 PLO-Israeli peace deal.
Saudi Arabia pledged $100 million as part of the international donor states' support for development of the Palestinian economy, so far delivering around $30 million.
